metadata.rules_text:
- Overestimate prices after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward quickly.
- Underestimate prices during negative sentiment periods; model reacts too slowly to bearish sentiment signals.
- Mean reversion bias: model often holds prices too high after strong upward moves, ignoring recent downward momentum.
- Lagged response to sentiment: model delays adjusting forecasts when sentiment turns negative, especially after 3–5 days of negative sentiment.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) and underestimate later (last 10–15 days), especially when sentiment is neutral or mildly bearish.
- Spike correction lag: after a price spike, model fails to reduce forecast quickly — often retains peak value for 3–5 days beyond true price drop.
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: when sentiment is negative (avg < 0.0), reduce forecast by 5–15% of recent peak; when sentiment is positive (avg > 0.3), increase by 5–10% only if recent price is rising.
